mind_map.root_node: Racing Seconds (Sexagesimal Time Units, Clock Translations & Elapsed Duration)

key_nodes: Base-60 Scale Factor: 1 Minute = 60 Seconds; 1 Hour = 60 Minutes = 3,600 Seconds
Minutes to Seconds: Multiply minutes by 60 (e.g., 4 min x 60 = 240 sec)
Seconds to Minutes: Divide seconds by 60 (e.g., 180 sec / 60 = 3 min)
Mixed Unit Conversion: Expressing 2 min 15 sec = (2 x 60) + 15 = 135 seconds
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Using base-10 (100) conversions for time instead of base-60 (e.g., thinking 1 min = 100 sec).
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Base-60 Time Rule: Multiply by 60 to move down unit hierarchy; divide by 60 to move up.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Timing 100m sprint races, cooking timers, and athletic sports training.

key_nodes: Digital Stopwatch Precision: Tracking hundredths of a second in sprint finish lines
Fractional Minute Benchmarks: 1/2 min = 30 sec; 1/4 min = 15 sec; 3/4 min = 45 sec
Comparing Race Split Times: Lower stopwatch reading indicates faster performance
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Thinking a larger stopwatch decimal value represents a faster runner.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Race Winner Rule: Smallest elapsed time = Fastest runner.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Olympic athletic track timing, swimming competitions, and motor racing split times.

key_nodes: 12-Hour Clock Structure: 12-hour cycle repeated twice daily (AM and PM)
AM (Ante Meridiem): Midnight (12:00 AM) to Noon (11:59 AM)
PM (Post Meridiem): Noon (12:00 PM) to Midnight (11:59 PM)
Ambiguity Risk: Missing AM/PM designation causes 12-hour scheduling errors
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Labeling 12:00 Noon as 12:00 AM or 12:00 Midnight as 12:00 PM.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Meridiem Rule: 12:00 Noon = 12:00 PM; 12:00 Midnight = 12:00 AM.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Setting alarm clocks and scheduling daily school appointments.

key_nodes: 24-Hour Railway Clock: 4-digit notation eliminating AM/PM confusion (00:00 = Midnight, 12:00 = Noon, 14:30 = 2:30 PM)
12-Hour PM to 24-Hour Conversion: Add 12 to hour digit (e.g., 7:45 PM + 12 = 19:45 hours)
24-Hour to 12-Hour Conversion: Subtract 12 from hours >= 13:00 (e.g., 21:15 - 12 = 9:15 PM)
Midnight & Noon Notation: 00:00 hours = Midnight; 12:00 hours = Noon
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Adding 12 to morning AM times when converting to 24-hour railway clock format.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Reading train timetables, flight departure boards, and television broadcast guides.

key_nodes: Elapsed Duration Formula: Duration = End Time - Start Time
Cross-Hour Regrouping: When subtracting minutes, borrow 1 hour as 60 minutes (not 100 minutes)
Adding Time Durations: Sum minutes; if total >= 60, convert 60 min to 1 hour
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Borrowing 100 minutes during time subtraction instead of 60 minutes.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Duration Identity: Duration = End_time - Start_time (regrouping 1 hr = 60 min).
sub_branches.real_world_application: Calculating movie length, exam durations, and school daily timetables.

key_nodes: Standard Calendar Year: 365 days; 52 weeks + 1 day
Leap Year Cycle: Every 4 years, February has 29 days (366 total days)
Leap Year Rule: Year divisible by 4 is a leap year (except century years not divisible by 400)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Assuming February always has 28 days every year.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Planning long-term project deadlines and calendar scheduling.
